messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a targeted benchmark comparing kernel-selector changes with q4f16 quant profile across two seq-shape mixes. observed a p99 regression on the mixed workload (~+120ms). attaching notes + commands below. :eyes:
steven: can you paste the exact numbers and the bench flags you used?
maria: sure — p50 ~ unchanged, p95 +30ms, p99 +120ms. throughput down ~4% on the mixed short/long workload. command: `./bench/run --profile q4f16 --kern auto --mix short:0.6,long:0.4 --warm-kv true --concurrency 16`
jun: was the KV cache warm consistently? that changes fusion behavior a lot.
maria: ran both. with kv-warm=true the regressions exist but are smaller. with cold-cache p99 +220ms and we saw kernel fallback events spike (~12% of requests fell back to generic kernel for certain long inputs).
alexa: did you diff outputs? could this be numerical drift from quant kernels vs fallback?
maria: did basic checks: token-level logprobs and top-5 token diffs. most inputs <1e-5 diff, but ~3% of long sequences had token-prob diffs >1e-3 and a couple had repeated-token artifacts when fallback happened mid-request.
perf-bot: automated summary for run 1972102468: p50=18ms p95=48ms p99=172ms throughput=980 req/s fallback_rate=12% artifacts_detected=2
amelia: my 2¢ — I think our bench sampling is the issue. the synthetic 60/40 mix isn't preserving real prefix length correlations. we should add a "per-client prefix-preserving" sampler and emit seq-shape histogram with every run.
sre-bot: note: rollout policy currently uses total throughput + error-rate. suggest adding p99-delta and fallback-rate gates; auto-rollback if p99 delta >50ms for >5m.
steven: can we capture a minimal reproducer? maybe a small set of long-prefix traces that force the fallback path. once we have that we can bisect kernel-change commits.
jun: i'll run an expanded sweep: vary concurrency (8/16/32), warm vs cold kv, and kernel=auto|force-optimized|force-generic. will log seq-shape histograms and top-k diffs. where should I drop the artifacts?
maria: put raw outputs and histograms in s3://redwood-bench/seqshape/1972102468/ and add a short gist with the failing traces. also add a CSV with per-request metrics.
alexa: propose tightening our correctness checks in bench harness: require max top-1 token-prob diff <1e-3 and entropy-delta <0.05, plus a greedy-match metric to catch repetition. failing runs should fail CI.
amelia: also add a microbench with KV-warm-start: `./bench/micro --kv-warm --repeat 1000 --seq long` to isolate attention kernel performance without routing noise.
steven: agreed. let's also add a note to the kernel-selection RFC follow-up: define acceptance gates for any kernel change: sampling mix, kv-warm/cold matrices, output-diff thresholds, fallback-rate cap (<=2%), and p99 throughput windows.
jun: i'll schedule the sweep and post results by EOD tomorrow. volunteers for bisect if I find a reg?
maria: i can take bisect if jun finds a candidate commit. tagging @jun @steven @alexa for follow-ups. :shipit:
perf-bot: bench run queued: expanded-sweep-1972102468 by jun — will post aggregated results when complete.
steven: nice work. one more ask — can we add seq-shape distributions to the perf dashboard so regressions include that context? current p99 alone is ambiguous.
amelia: agreed. adding a dashboard tile: seq-length histogram + fallback-rate timeline next to latency percentiles.
sre-bot: i've added an alert rule: if fallback_rate >5% AND p99 delta >30ms for >10m, page oncall.
maria: thanks all. next steps: jun runs sweep, artifacts to s3 path above, alexa will propose exact bench harness thresholds in PR, steven will update RFC gates, amelia will add dashboard tile, sre-bot added alerts. closing loop after sweep results. :thinking_face:
